verses.text: Of the sons of Issachar: Tola, and Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their fathers’ houses, of Tola; mighty men of valor in their generations. Their number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five; all of them chief men.
With them, by their generations, after their fathers’ houses, were bands of the army for war, thirty-six thousand; for they had many wives and sons.
Their brothers among all the families of Issachar, mighty men of valor, listed in all by genealogy, were eighty-seven thousand.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, five; heads of fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor; and they were listed by genealogy twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Becher.
They were listed by genealogy, after their generations, heads of their fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor, twenty thousand two hundred.
The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these were sons of Jediael, according to the heads of their fathers’ households, mighty men of valor, seventeen thousand two hundred, who were able to go out in the army for war.
So were Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, and the sons of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bore. She bore Machir the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister’s name was Maacah. The name of the second was Zelophehad; and Zelophehad had daughters.
Maacah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she named him Peresh. The name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath who were born in the land killed, because they came down to take away their livestock.
Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He went in to his wife, and she conceived, and bore a son, and he named him Beriah,  because there was trouble with his house.
His daughter was Sheerah, who built Beth Horon the lower and the upper, and Uzzen Sheerah.
Rephah was his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, and Joshua his son.
Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with its towns; Shechem also and its towns, to Azzah and its towns;
and by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth Shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, and Dor and its towns. The children of Joseph the son of Israel lived in these.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah was their sister.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.

All these were the children of Asher, heads of the fathers’ houses, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes. The number of them listed by genealogy for service in war was twenty-six thousand men.

footnotes.content: The sons of Issachar are named first—Tola, Puah, Jashub, Shimron. Four brothers, four lines of blessing branching out. It strikes me that the recorder noticed them all, gave each a name that would echo through generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tola's line produced twenty-two thousand six hundred mighty men by David's day—strength multiplied through faithfulness. The Lord loves to take one faithful person's legacy and make it a multitude.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five sons to Izrahiah, all chiefs. The text marks them as leaders—not by accident, but by the Lord's design. A father watches his children step into responsibility and sees the hand of God at work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty-six thousand warriors, because "they had many wives and sons." The blessing of a full house, a thriving line. The Lord fills what He ordains, and abundance flows through generations when family is treasured.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eighty-seven thousand total—Issachar's whole roll listed by genealogy. Not forgotten, not lost in the crowd. Every name written down, every line accounted for. The God who knows the stars by name knows us too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benjamin's three sons begin now—Bela, Becher, Jediael. Three branches from one strong trunk. Even in a genealogy, you feel the family tree growing, each generation another layer of roots and fruit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bela's line produced twenty-two thousand thirty-four warriors—"mighty men of valor." Courage is a legacy that runs in families, drawn up from faith deeper than the grave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nine sons to Becher, each name distinct: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, Alemeth. Nine voices, nine choices, nine chances to bring honor or shame to the house. The Lord sees each one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty thousand two hundred mighty men from Becher's house. When faithfulness runs through a line unbroken, it multiplies in strength—not by conquest, but by the blessing of the Lord who holds all generations in His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jediael's son Bilhan, and Bilhan's seven sons—Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, Ahishahar. Generations flowing onward, names preserved, stories carried forward by those who came after.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seventeen thousand two hundred warriors, able to march to war. Behind every number stands a person—a son, a father, a man who stood firm when faithfulness was tested.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, the sons of Aher—names we scarce know, yet the chronicler wrote them all. The Lord's memory is perfect; no faithful servant is ever truly forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naphtali's sons: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and the sons of Bilhah—the maidservant's children carried forward through generations. The Lord lifted up the lowly and made them a people; no birth is beneath His notice or care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manasseh's son Asriel, born of an Aramean concubine. And Machir—he became the father of Gilead, whose very name would mark a place of balm, of healing. Sometimes the Lord writes a legacy in geography, in the land itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Machir took a wife and built a house. Zelophehad is named—a man whose daughters would one day go before the Lord seeking their inheritance, teaching Israel that the Lord honors the courageous plea for justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Maacah bore Peresh and Sheresh, and their sons Ulam and Rakem. A mother's name preserved forever alongside her sons'—the Lord sees the woman who bears and raises up the next generation with quiet faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bedan, son of Ulam—the line continues, each generation a link in an unbroken chain stretching back to Jacob and forward to God's purpose. We are never alone; we inherit the faith of those before us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hammolecheth, sister and mother to Ishhod, Abiezer, Mahlah. Her sons bore great names—Abiezer the mighty, names that speak of God's help. A sister's blessing flows through generations she will never see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shemida's four sons: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, Aniam. Shechem—a place and a name, rooted deep in Israel's story. The Lord writes history through families, weaves lives into the very land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephraim's line opens: Shuthelah, then Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath again—generations traced careful and complete. Each name a heartbeat in the great story of Israel's survival and God's faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezer and Elead, killed by men of Gath for cattle. Tragedy strikes even within the people of God—theft, violence, sons cut down in their youth. Yet the Lord's story does not end in death; it ends in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephraim mourned many days for his slain sons. His brothers came to comfort him—a picture of the body grieving, standing with one another in loss. Jesus wept; so do His people, and so can we.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Then Ephraim conceived again, named his new son Beriah—"because there was trouble with his house." From sorrow comes another son, another chance, another mercy. The Lord turns mourning into His strange comfort.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His daughter Sheerah built Beth Horon the lower and upper, and Uzzen Sheerah. A woman's work in stone, her engineering skill recorded alongside the men's. The Lord delights to see His daughters build, strengthen, leave a mark on the land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rephah, Resheph, Telah, Tahan—the line branches again through generations. Each father names his son, each son becomes a father in turn, the covenant passed forward like a torch through the darkness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ladan, Ammihud, Elishama—Elishama's name speaks of God hearing. In names, Israel testified: the Lord hears our cry, sees our plight, remembers us. That same God hears His people still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nun, and his son Joshua. There it is—the great Joshua, who led Israel into the promised land, springs from this line. One man's faithfulness shaped a nation's crossing; the Lord crowns with honor those who serve Him wholly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bethel, Naaran, Gezer, Shechem, Azzah—the land itself held by Ephraim. These towns map the territory promised, settled, held by faith. Geography becomes theology when we see the Lord's faithfulness written across the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, Dor—ancient strongholds, places where Israel's story unfolded. "The children of Joseph lived in these." The God who promised the land brought them safe to its fulfillment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asher's four sons and a sister: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, Serah. Serah named alongside the brothers—the chronicler was careful to mark her. She belonged fully to the people, counted as one of them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beriah's sons: Heber and Malchiel, Malchiel the father of Birzaith. The genealogy grows dense now, but each name tells of lives lived, choices made, blessings given and received.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua. Four siblings, one family bearing the name forward. The Lord loves to see families knit together in love and faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Japhlet's sons: Pasach, Bimhal, Ashvath. Three more branches, three more sets of descendants who would inherit the faith of their fathers and pass it on or set it aside.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shemer's sons: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, Aram. Four names, and in each a story the recorder thought worth keeping. Not all deeds are recorded in Scripture, but none are forgotten by the One who knows all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Helem's sons: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, Amal. Four more branches of the great tree, each one tender with possibility, each one held in the hand of the God who ordained them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zophah's many sons: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, Beera—a great flock of children, each one precious, each one known by name to the Lord who formed them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jether's sons: Jephunneh, Pispa, Ara. Three more, the line continuing, generation after generation in an endless chain reaching toward eternity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ulla's sons: Arah, Hanniel, Rizia. Three more voices, three more names pressed into the page by the chronicler's careful hand, as if to say: they mattered, and God remembers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "All these were the children of Asher...twenty-six thousand men." Readers today hear an echo in these genealogies: we too are numbered, known by the Father, counted among His people. We don't just survive—we thrive, multiplying in faithful generations as we trust in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
